# Mission: sweep of 16 poles

Colour in 16 random poles that have no record yet, about 2 minutes each. One branch, one pre-registration commit,
one batch run, one PR. No claims: a pole someone else also tests gets two independent results, which is good.

1. Branch: git checkout -b sweep/moridinamael-2026-10-18-1741
2. Draw and create the tests files: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play draw --k 16 --handle moridinamael
   (writes one tests file per pole and lists them in .sweep/latest.txt; work on exactly those files,
   e.g. git add --pathspec-from-file=.sweep/latest.txt and play run --list .sweep/latest.txt; both work in any shell)
3. Read every card in one call: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play card --neuron <id1> <id2> … --out cards.txt   (no GPU: examples, density, flags,
   logit effect; one call loads the scan and weights once; then read cards.txt, which is not committed)
   If it is unclear, try a few sentences: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play probe --neuron <id> "…" "…"
   Label at the level the card supports: usually a token or a context. A pole the card flags dense or positional
   gets "unit_kind": "dense / positional" (a top-level key in its tests file) and a test of your best guess at what drives it.
   It will probably fail; its job is to record the density honestly, not to find a meaning.
   To try sentences on many poles with one model load: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play probe --plan plan.json
   (plan.json: {"<pole id>": ["sentence", ...], ...}). Each tests file is for ONE pole, the one in its "neuron" field.
4. Pre-register all of them. Each pole needs a label, 8 fire sentences and 8 near misses (same topic and style, without the trigger).
   Easiest: write one plan.json and run uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play fill --plan plan.json --agent "<who you are>"
   plan.json: {"<pole id>": {"label": "...", "fire": [8 sentences], "quiet": [8 near misses], "short": "2-5 words",
   "unit_kind": "lexical|contextual|sparse feature|dense|positional|unclear", "confidence": 0.6, "notes": "..."}, ...}
   (fill writes LF line endings, removes the template's reference list and refuses wrong keys). Or edit the files directly:
   methods.agent (who you are) and methods.screens (e.g. card, probe). quick-8+8@2 judges each: AUROC >= 0.90,
   median fire >= 0.20 of the pole's max, at most 1 near miss >= 0.30.
   Optional keys: notes, short, unit_kind, confidence, predictions. Delete _screens_vocabulary (it is only a reference list)
   and any optional key you leave unfilled.
   Commit ALL tests files together and ALONE: git add --pathspec-from-file=.sweep/latest.txt && git commit -m "Pre-register sweep tests"
5. Run them all at once (one model load): uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play run --list .sweep/latest.txt
   Commit the results SEPARATELY: git add graph/contributions && git commit -m "Sweep results: <held>/<total> held"
6. Validate (uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.validate), push, and open one PR:
   mkdir -p .pr && cp .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/interpret.md .pr/sweep-moridinamael-2026-10-18-1741.md (gitignored; fill it in, one line per pole: id, label, outcome), then
   git push -u origin sweep/moridinamael-2026-10-18-1741 && gh pr create --repo moridinamael/bonsai-interp --title "sweep: 16 poles (<held> held)" --body-file .pr/sweep-moridinamael-2026-10-18-1741.md
   The merge agent merges conforming PRs once the checks pass, and regenerates the map.

Failed labels are results too; record them and move on. Do not re-test inside a sweep: a second round is a new mission.

Rules (from AGENTS.md; once CI is enabled it enforces 1-3, and play run already refuses uncommitted tests):
1. Commit the .tests.json ON ITS OWN before running anything that scores it; results go in a SECOND commit. Never amend, squash or edit a committed .tests.json.
2. Never edit or delete files under graph/contributions/ (yours included). Do not commit graph/neurons, edges.json or index.json: the merge agent regenerates them on main after merging.
3. Only the two contribution files (<= 64 KB each) go in git; bulky material goes to the library (DATA_POLICY.md).
4. Report honestly: a failed label is a valid contribution. Do not rewrite a test after seeing its result.

When done, tell the person in two or three sentences what you found and give them the PR link.

# Instructions for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, â€¦)

You are helping a person contribute to the **Bonsai Neuron Survey**, an open, test-backed map of
what each neuron in Bonsai-8B does. Bonsai-8B is a 1-bit language model with 36 layers and
12,288 MLP neurons per layer, and each neuron has a + and a âˆ’ pole. The person usually pasted a
prompt from the survey page. Your job is to do the work end to end on their machine and stop
only for things only they can do.

Run every Python command through the project environment: `uv run python -m â€¦`, or
`.venv/Scripts/python` on Windows, `.venv/bin/python` elsewhere.

## 1. Get ready (once per machine)

You need about 3 GB of disk in total: 1.2 GB of weights and 1.4 GB of data. The scripts are
bash; on Windows, Git Bash (which comes with Git for Windows) runs them.

Hardware: an NVIDIA GPU with 8 GB or more (a mission peaks at about 5 GB), or an Apple Silicon Mac (macOS 14 or later; 32 GB
of unified memory recommended, 16 GB is tight). The toolchain picks the device itself (CUDA,
then Apple's MPS, then the CPU). To force one, put `BONSAI_DEVICE=cuda`, `mps` or `cpu` in
`.env`. The CPU is fine for checks but too slow for missions. Mac details are in the README
under "Running on a Mac".

1. Clone https://github.com/moridinamael/neuron-cleanroom next to this repository; blind
   clean-room missions need it. Ask the person for their GitHub handle now, since every
   mission uses it.
2. Install the environment: `uv sync`. You need Python 3.11â€“3.13 and uv. If uv is missing,
   install it from https://docs.astral.sh/uv/.
3. Get the model weights (Bonsai-8B only):
   - If they are **already on this machine**, put `BONSAI1_PATH=<that folder>` in `.env`
     instead of downloading. The folder is the one that contains `config.json` and either the
     `model-0000x-of-00004.safetensors` shards or `Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf`.
   - Otherwise run `bash scripts/download_models.sh`. It fetches PrismML's 1-bit GGUF (1.2 GB),
     which holds exactly the same weights as the 16 GB unpacked release. A warning about unauthenticated Hugging Face requests is harmless.
4. Fetch the data: `bash scripts/fetch_data.sh`. It downloads the corpus (120 MB), the full
   neuron scan (1.1 GB) and a band scan (0.2 GB), and needs `gh` to be logged in.
5. Run `python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play doctor` and fix whatever it reports, until it says
   **READY**. Doctor checks every weight shard, then loads the model and reads one known neuron.
   It reports the device and its speed, and it compares the reading with the reference CUDA
   machine. On a device other than CUDA, also run `uv run python tests/test_device_parity.py`
   once. It checks four neurons, the model's next-token prediction and the backward pass, and it
   must print PARITY OK.
6. **Ask the person** only for things you cannot do yourself:
   - logging in to GitHub (`gh auth login`)
   - a globalMOO key, which is optional and goes in `.env` as `GMOO_API_KEY=â€¦`
   - permission to use the disk space
   - for blind missions, the `claude` CLI or `codex` CLI

When everything passes, tell the person "Ready to survey". Report the GPU and anything optional
that is missing.

## 2. Play a mission

The survey page gives the person a one-line prompt containing a mission, such as `interpret
bonsai1/L12/N5397-`. Turn it into a full brief and follow that:

```
python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play brief <interpret|qc|step|blind> --neuron <id> --handle <github handle> [--gmoo]
```

The brief is generated from this repository, so it always matches the current pipeline. Follow
it in order.

## 3. Rules you must not break

1. **Pre-register.** Write the test (label, 8 sentences that should fire the pole, and 8 near
   misses) and **commit it on its own before running anything that scores it**. Then run
   and commit the results (contribution files only) in a **second** commit. Never amend or squash those two commits
   together, and never edit a committed `.tests.json`. CI checks all of this.
2. **Append-only.** Never edit or delete anyone's files under `graph/contributions/`, including
   your own earlier ones. A correction is a new contribution.
3. **PRs carry contributions only.** Never commit `graph/neurons/`, `graph/edges.json` or
   `graph/index.json`: the merge agent regenerates them on `main` after each merge. You may run
   `python -m bonsai_interp.graph.fold` locally to preview the record, but don't commit the output.
4. **Data policy** ([DATA_POLICY.md](DATA_POLICY.md)):
   - Only the two contribution files go in git, at most 64 KB each.
   - Banks, logs and transcripts go to the library and are referenced by hash.
   - Never commit tensors, weights, `.env`, keys or local paths.
5. **globalMOO.** Use at most one globalMOO model per neuron, and only if the person supplied a
   key. Use SciPy for everything else.
6. **No claims.** Contributions never conflict, so nobody reserves a pole. If two people test the
   same one, both results count, and the second is an independent replication.
7. **Record your methods.** Fill `methods.agent` (who did the work, e.g. "claude-code opus-5.5") and
   `methods.screens` (the analyses you used, from `bonsai_interp/graph/methods.py`) in the tests file.
   `play run` adds what it can detect and the time taken. This is how the survey learns which
   techniques pay off.
8. **Report honestly.** A failed label is a valid contribution. Do not rewrite the test after
   seeing the result. If you want a better label, that is a new round with new sentences.

## 4. Doing the science well

- **Explore with `play probe`.** It scores any sentences on a pole without recording anything:
  `python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play probe --neuron <id> "sentence" â€¦`. If you write your own
  scripts, run them from the repository root with `PYTHONPATH=.` so `bonsai_interp` imports.
- **Start from the card.** `play card --neuron <id>` shows both poles' top examples, how dense the
  pole is, its sign regimes and the tokens its output promotes, and flags dense or positional units,
  in seconds and without the GPU. `play which "text"` goes the other way: which poles fire on each
  token of your text (`--token " nerve"` for poles whose top examples peak on one token).
- **Look widely before you label.** Read the top examples with `play look`. Then look at weak
  and middle activations and at which tokens fire the pole most *often* (`bonsai_interp.probe.bands`).
  The flagship example: the "nerve" neuron's commonest strong trigger was " strong".
- **Label at the level your test can support:**
  - a word ("the token ' disconnect'")
  - a context ("'to' after an eagerness predicate")
  - a topic or meaning

  Test the meaning without the word, and the word without the meaning, before you claim a
  meaning.
- **Near misses carry the test.** They keep the topic, length and style, and drop only the
  claimed trigger. Easy near misses (unrelated filler) make a label look cleaner than it is.
- **Neurons can be dense.** Some are on for most text, and an 8 + 8 test cannot pass for them.
  Say so with `"unit_kind": "dense / positional"` instead of forcing a label.
- **Write your own sentences.** If the model wrote them, run with `--author bonsai`, because
  model-written near misses misfire more often.

## 5. Finish

Open the PR with the right shape:

```
gh pr create --repo moridinamael/bonsai-interp --template interpret.md   # or qc.md
```

Fill in the template. List the two commit hashes in order and include the one-line result.
Then tell the person what you found in two or three sentences, and give them the PR link.
# What goes in the repo, what goes in the library, and what goes nowhere

The repo must stay small enough to clone in seconds while the graph grows to thousands of
neurons. A quick-tested neuron costs about 16 KB here. A fully probed neuron produces 1â€“5 MB of
files, almost all of it solver logs and generated HTML. So git holds the **evidence and the
recipe**; everything bulky lives in the **library** and is referenced by hash.

## 1. In git: the evidence and the recipe

Each contribution is at most two files and **64 KB per file**. A PR adds at most **256 KB under
`graph/`**, and CI enforces both limits.

| What | Why it is in git |
|---|---|
| The pre-registration (`<id>.tests.json`): label, the 8 + 8 test sentences, predictions | It *is* the test. Its commit date is the proof it came first |
| The results (`<id>.json`): counts, per-sentence activation and peak token (3 decimals), outcome | Small, and what reviewers read |
| Edges found while stepping out (`from`, `to`, `kind`, `weight`, `method`) | They are the graph |
| The recipe: toolchain commit, command, seed | Anything here can be recomputed from it |
| Up to 8 corpus examples, at most 400 characters each | Enough to see the job; corpus text stays under its own licence |
| Notes, at most 4,000 characters | Longer write-ups go in the library |

Neuron records (`graph/neurons/`), `graph/edges.json` and `graph/index.json` are **derived** by
`python -m bonsai_interp.graph.fold`. Nobody edits them by hand.

## 2. In the library: bulky, optional, referenced by hash

Put large or numerous artefacts in the library and list them in your contribution's `artifacts`:

```json
"artifacts": [{"name": "bank.json", "url": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/<org>/bonsai-interp-library/resolve/main/<id>/bank.json",
               "sha256": "â€¦", "bytes": 174612}]
```

Examples:
- sentence banks larger than the test sets
- inverse-solver evaluation logs
- band samples
- steering generations
- clean-room transcripts and room bundles
- HTML dossiers and figures

The library is a Hugging Face dataset repository: versioned, built for large files, and free.
The merge agent checks that each URL resolves and that its hash matches. A missing library file
never invalidates a contribution, because git already holds the evidence.

## 3. Nowhere

- **Activation vectors, tensors, scans or caches.** Recompute them from the recipe. If one is
  essential to a claim, upload it to the library and explain why.
- **Model weights, or copies of the corpus.** They are on Hugging Face and in the `data-v1`
  release.
- **Secrets** (`.env`, API keys, tokens), **local paths**, and personal data about anyone.
- **Long copied text**: corpus excerpts over 400 characters, or third-party documents.

## Why this split

- **Reproducible:** every number in git has a recipe. Anyone with the model can regenerate the
  bulky parts, so storing them is a convenience, not a requirement.
- **Reviewable:** a PR is a few kilobytes of JSON that a person or an agent can read in full.
- **Bounded:** at about 16 KB per quick-tested neuron, 10,000 neurons is about 150 MB of git.
  The library grows without slowing anyone's clone.

"""Which agents, screens and toolchains produced a contribution, so the survey can learn which
techniques pay off (`python -m bonsai_interp.graph.meta`).

Every new contribution carries a "methods" block:

  {"agent": "claude-code opus-5.5" | "codex gpt-6.1" | "human" | ...,
   "screens": ["look", "bands", "probe", "quick-test", ...],   declared by the contributor, plus
   "detected": [...],                                          what play run could see on disk
   "toolchain_commit": "...", "harness": "neuron-cleanroom@..." (blind runs),
   "minutes": 37}                                              pre-registration commit -> results

SCREENS is the shared vocabulary. Unknown screen names are allowed (new tools arrive by PR) but
reported, so the vocabulary can be extended in the same PR that adds the tool.
"""
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

SCREENS = {
    "look": "top corpus examples (play look / explore)",
    "bands": "full activation distribution and band samples (probe.bands)",
    "probe": "exploratory sentence scoring, nothing recorded (play probe)",
    "card": "neuron card: top examples, density, regimes, logit effect, flags (play card)",
    "which": "reverse search: which poles fire on a text or token (play which)",
    "quick-test": "pre-registered 8 + 8 sentence test (quick-8+8)",
    "second-round": "a further labelling round after a failed test",
    "step-out": "strongest feeders by attribution + single-unit zeroing (play step), edges recorded",
    "bank-solo": "sentence bank with competing hypotheses, dose-response (probe.run solo)",
    "held-out": "pre-registered held-out set (held-out protocol)",
    "inverse-de": "text-level inverse with SciPy differential evolution (probe.run invert --solver de)",
    "inverse-gmoo": "text-level inverse with a globalMOO learned model (probe.run invert --solver gmoo)",
    "induce": "steering the neuron and reading output effects (probe.run induce)",
    "neighbors": "upstream / disambiguator / downstream map (probe.neighbors)",
    "disproof": "corpus-wide attempts to break the label (frequency tables, band annotation, leak search)",
    "blind-room": "investigation by a blind agent in a clean room (neuron-cleanroom)",
    "atlas": "word x frame x language fingerprint",
}


def detect(root: Path, L: int, n: int, pole: str) -> list:
    """Screens whose traces for this neuron exist in this checkout (probe files, band scans)."""
    found = []
    d = root / "probes" / f"bonsai1_L{L}_N{n}_{'pos' if pole == '+' else 'neg'}"
    files = {p.name for p in d.glob("*")} if d.exists() else set()
    for screen, names in (("bank-solo", {"bank.json", "solo.json"}), ("held-out", {"holdout.json"}),
                          ("inverse-de", {"invert_de.json"}), ("inverse-gmoo", {"invert_gmoo.json"}),
                          ("induce", {"induce.json"}), ("neighbors", {"neighbors.json"}), ("look", {"forward.json"})):
        if files & names:
            found.append(screen)
    import zipfile
    for npz in (root / "data").glob("bands_*.npz"):
        try:
            if f"L{L}_N{n}.npy" in zipfile.ZipFile(npz).namelist():
                found.append("bands")
                break
        except zipfile.BadZipFile:
            pass
    return sorted(set(found))


def minutes_between(root: Path, tests_rel: str) -> int | None:
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "log", "--diff-filter=A", "--format=%ct", "--", tests_rel], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
    if not out:
        return None
    import time
    return round((time.time() - int(out[-1])) / 60)

def fill(a):
    """Fill tests files from one JSON plan: {"<pole id>": {"label": ..., "fire": [8], "quiet": [8], optional keys}, ...}.
    Writes LF line endings, drops the template's reference list, and refuses anything it cannot place."""
    plan = json.loads(Path(a.plan).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    files = [ln.strip() for ln in Path(a.list).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    by_pole = {}
    for f in files:
        t = json.loads((ROOT / f).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        by_pole[t["neuron"]] = (f, t)
    unknown = [k for k in plan if k not in by_pole]
    if unknown:
        sys.exit(f"plan has poles that are not in {a.list}: {unknown}")
    done = []
    for nid, e in plan.items():
        f, t = by_pole[nid]
        bad = [k for k in e if k not in ("label", "fire", "quiet", "agent", "screens", *OPTIONAL)]
        if bad or len(e.get("fire", [])) != 8 or len(e.get("quiet", [])) != 8 or not e.get("label"):
            sys.exit(f"{nid}: needs label, 8 fire and 8 quiet sentences; optional keys {sorted(OPTIONAL)}; unknown keys {bad}")
        nb = t["neighbours"][0]
        nb.update(label=e["label"], fire=e["fire"], quiet=e["quiet"])
        for k in OPTIONAL:
            if k in e:
                t[k] = e[k]
        if t.get("predictions", "").startswith("<optional"):
            t.pop("predictions")
        m = t.setdefault("methods", {})
        m.pop("_screens_vocabulary", None)
        if e.get("agent") or a.agent:
            m["agent"] = e.get("agent") or a.agent
        if e.get("screens"):
            m["screens"] = e["screens"]
        (ROOT / f).write_text(json.dumps(t, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        done.append(f)
    left = [f for p, (f, _) in by_pole.items() if p not in plan]
    print(f"filled {len(done)} tests files" + (f"; not in the plan yet: {left}" if left else "; every listed file is filled"))


def _check_tests_file(path):
    """(problem or None, tests dict, rel path, prereg commit) for one pre-registration."""
    p = Path(path).resolve()
    rel = p.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
    t = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    templates = set(TEMPLATE_FIRE + TEMPLATE_QUIET + ["<your label>"])
    left = [s for nb in t["neighbours"] for s in nb["fire"] + nb["quiet"] + [nb["label"]] if s in templates]
    if left:
        return f"{rel}: still has {len(left)} template placeholder(s), e.g. {left[0]!r}", None, rel, None
    agent = (t.get("methods") or {}).get("agent")
    if not agent or str(agent).startswith("<who did the work"):
        return f"{rel}: fill in methods.agent (who did the work), commit, then run", None, rel, None
    if subprocess.run(["git", "log", "--format=%h", "-1", "--", rel], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip() == "":
        return f"{rel}: content OK; not committed yet: commit the pre-registration first", None, rel, None
    if subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--quiet", "HEAD", "--", rel], cwd=ROOT).returncode != 0:
        return f"{rel}: has uncommitted edits; a pre-registration must be run exactly as committed", None, rel, None
    prereg = subprocess.run(["git", "log", "--diff-filter=A", "--format=%h", "--", rel], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()[-1]
    return None, t, rel, prereg


def run(a):
    """Score one or more committed pre-registrations with ONE model load (batching is where the time goes:
    loading takes 30-60 s, a 16-sentence test about a second)."""
    files = list(a.tests_files) + ([ln.strip() for ln in Path(a.list).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if ln.strip()] if a.list else [])
    if not files:
        sys.exit("give tests files, or --list <file with one per line>")
    checked = [(f, *_check_tests_file(f)) for f in files]
    problems = [c[1] for c in checked if c[1]]
    for msg in problems:
        print("SKIP", msg)
    todo = [c for c in checked if not c[1]]
    if not todo:
        sys.exit("nothing to run")
    import torch
    from bonsai_interp import explore
    from bonsai_interp.env import limit_memory
    from bonsai_interp.model import load
    from bonsai_interp.probe import textinv
    limit_memory(0.8)
    models, scans = {}, {}
    for f, _, t, rel, prereg in todo:
        m = NEURON.match(t["neuron"])
        if m["model"] not in models:
            models[m["model"]] = load(m["model"])
            models[m["model"]][1].padding_side = "right"
            scans[m["model"]] = explore.scan(m["model"])
        model, tok, rec = models[m["model"]]
        scan = scans[m["model"]]
        tests = []
        for nb in t["neighbours"]:
            L, n = map(int, nb["unit"][1:].split("/N"))
            pole = 0 if nb["pole"] == "+" else 1
            pmax, omax = float(scan["top_val"][L, pole, 0, n]), float(scan["top_val"][L, 1 - pole, 0, n])
            ev = textinv.TextEvaluator(model, tok, rec, L, n, pmax, omax, 1.0 if pole == 0 else -1.0)
            fire, quiet = ev(nb["fire"]), ev(nb["quiet"])
            per = [{"set": s, "i": i, "act": round(r["act"], 3), "peak": r["peak_token"]} for s, rs in (("fire", fire), ("quiet", quiet)) for i, r in enumerate(rs)]
            nf, fp = sum(r["act"] >= 0.3 for r in fire), sum(r["act"] >= 0.3 for r in quiet)
            test = {"protocol": t["protocol"], "tests_file": rel, "prereg_commit": prereg, "author": a.author or t["contributor"],
                    "n_fire": nf, "n_false_pos": fp, "n_written": [len(fire), len(quiet)], "per_sentence": per}
            tests.append(test)
            from bonsai_interp.graph.protocols import v2_stats
            auroc, med, _ = v2_stats(test)  # the recorded (rounded) values the rule judges, so print and verdict agree
            fa = [r["act"] for r in fire]
            print(f"{t['neuron']:<22} AUROC {auroc:.2f} (need >= 0.90), median fire {med:.2f} (need >= 0.20), "
                  f"near misses >= 0.30: {fp} (max 1); fire >= 0.30: {nf}/{len(fa)} -> {outcome(test).upper()} under {t['protocol']}"
                  if t["protocol"] == "quick-8+8@2" else
                  f"{t['neuron']:<22} {nb['unit']}{nb['pole']}: fire {nf}/{len(fire)}, near misses firing {fp}/{len(quiet)} "
                  f"-> {outcome(test).upper()} under {t['protocol']}")
        p = Path(f).resolve()
        declared = dict(t.get("methods") or {})
        declared.pop("_screens_vocabulary", None)
        tests_screens = ["quick-test"] + (["second-round"] if len(list(p.parent.glob("*.tests.json"))) > 1 else [])
        meth = {**declared, "screens": sorted(set(declared.get("screens", [])) | set(tests_screens)),
                "detected": detect(ROOT, int(m["L"]), int(m["n"]), m["pole"]), "toolchain_commit": _commit(),
                "minutes": minutes_between(ROOT, rel), "batch_size": len(todo)}
        unknown = [x for x in meth["screens"] if x not in SCREENS]
        if unknown:
            print(f"note: screens not in the shared vocabulary (add them in bonsai_interp/graph/methods.py): {unknown}")
        c = {"id": t["contribution"], "kind": t["kind"], "neuron": t["neuron"], "contributor": t["contributor"],
             "created": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
             "recipe": {"toolchain_commit": _commit(), "command": f"python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play run {rel}"},
             "label": t["neighbours"][0]["label"], "tests": tests, "methods": meth}
        if t["kind"] == "qc":
            c["qc"] = {"verdict": t["qc"]["verdict"], "label_under_test": t["qc"].get("label_under_test")}
            if t["qc"]["verdict"] != "refine":
                c.pop("label")
        for k in ("short", "unit_kind", "confidence", "notes", "roles", "via"):
            if t.get(k) is not None:
                c[k] = t[k]
        out = p.with_name(p.name.replace(".tests.json", ".json"))
        out.write_text(json.dumps(c, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        print(f"   wrote {out.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()}")
    print(f"\n{len(todo)} scored, {len(problems)} skipped. Commit the results files in a SEPARATE commit from the pre-registrations "
          f"and open a PR with only graph/contributions/ files (the merge agent regenerates the derived graph files).")

"""Neuron cards: a compact, label-free view of any of the 442,368 neurons, from the corpus scan and the weights.

  python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play card --neuron bonsai1/L9/N3688+ [--k 6] [--out card.json|card.md]

A card holds, for both poles: the top corpus examples with the peak token in ⟦ ⟧, the pole's corpus max,
its activation density (share of all scanned tokens above 0.1 and 0.3 of that max, read from the scan's
log-binned histograms), and the sign-regime split. It adds the direct logit effect of the neuron's output
direction (final norm gain, then the unembedding; weights only, read on the CPU) and flags for units an
8 + 8 test can't pass (dense, positional). No GPU and no model load: a card takes a few seconds.
"""
import json
from functools import lru_cache

import numpy as np

from bonsai_interp import explore
from bonsai_interp.graph.contrib import NEURON, ROOT

# flags (calibrated on the poles contributors marked dense / positional, against held token poles)
DENSE_10 = 0.10     # >= 10% of tokens above 0.1 of max: an 8 + 8 test can hardly pass
BROAD_10 = 0.01     # >= 1%: near misses will often fire weakly
POSITIONAL = 0.5    # >= half of the top 32 peaks within the first 16 tokens of a window, or one position


def parse(neuron):
    """'bonsai1/L9/N3688+' or 'L9/N3688' or '9/3688' -> (model, L, n, pole or None)."""
    m = NEURON.match(neuron)
    if m:
        return m["model"], int(m["L"]), int(m["n"]), m["pole"]
    s = neuron.removeprefix("bonsai1/").replace("L", "").replace("N", "")
    pole = s[-1] if s[-1] in "+-" else None
    L, n = map(int, s.rstrip("+-").split("/"))
    return "bonsai1", L, n, pole


def _above(h, lower, upper, t):
    """Count in a log-binned histogram above threshold t, splitting the straddling bin log-uniformly."""
    b = int(np.searchsorted(lower, t, side="right")) - 1  # lower[b] <= t < lower[b+1]
    n = h[b + 1:].sum()
    lo, hi = lower[b], upper[b]
    if lo > 0 and np.isfinite(hi) and hi > t:
        n += h[b] * (np.log(hi) - np.log(t)) / (np.log(hi) - np.log(lo))
    elif lo == 0 and hi > t:
        n += h[b] * (hi - t) / hi
    return float(n)


def pole_stats(name, L, n, pole):
    s = explore.scan(name)
    pi, regs = (0, [0, 1]) if pole == "+" else (1, [2, 3])
    mx = float(s["top_val"][L, pi, 0, n])
    h = s["hist"][L, n]  # (4 regimes, NB); bin b holds |a| in (bins[b-1], bins[b]]
    bins = s["bins"].astype(np.float64)
    lower, upper = np.concatenate([[0], bins]), np.concatenate([bins, [np.inf]])
    total = float(h.sum())
    pole_h = h[regs].sum(0)
    dens = {f: _above(pole_h, lower, upper, f * mx) / total for f in (0.1, 0.3)}
    split = {}
    for r in regs:  # regime shares among this pole's activations above 0.1 of max
        split[explore.REGIMES[r]] = _above(h[r], lower, upper, 0.1 * mx)
    tot = sum(split.values())
    split = {k: round(v / tot, 3) if tot else None for k, v in split.items()}
    pos = s["top_pos"][L, pi, :, n]
    pos = pos[np.isfinite(s["top_val"][L, pi, :, n])]
    vals, counts = np.unique(pos, return_counts=True)
    early, mode_share = float((pos < 16).mean()) if len(pos) else 0.0, float(counts.max() / len(pos)) if len(pos) else 0.0
    return {"max": round(mx, 3), "density": {"0.1": round(dens[0.1], 5), "0.3": round(dens[0.3], 5)},
            "regimes": split, "peak_positions": {"first16": round(early, 3), "commonest": int(vals[counts.argmax()]) if len(pos) else None,
                                                  "commonest_share": round(mode_share, 3)}}


def flags(st):
    out = []
    d = st["density"]["0.1"]
    if d >= DENSE_10:
        out.append(f"dense: {d:.1%} of tokens reach 0.1 of max; an 8 + 8 test can hardly pass (consider unit_kind 'dense / positional')")
    elif d >= BROAD_10:
        out.append(f"broad: {d:.1%} of tokens reach 0.1 of max; near misses will often fire weakly")
    pp = st["peak_positions"]
    if pp["first16"] >= POSITIONAL or pp["commonest_share"] >= POSITIONAL:
        out.append(f"positional: top peaks cluster at window position {pp['commonest']} "
                   f"({pp['commonest_share']:.0%}; {pp['first16']:.0%} within the first 16 tokens)")
    if st["regimes"]:
        echo = max(st["regimes"], key=lambda k: st["regimes"][k] or 0)
        if echo in ("-x- echo", "-g +u leak") and (st["regimes"][echo] or 0) >= 0.6:
            out.append(f"gate-closed regime dominates ({echo} {st['regimes'][echo]:.0%})")
    return out


@lru_cache(None)
def _weights(name):
    """(down_proj column reader, final norm gain in fp32, unembedding in fp16) on the CPU, from the
    unpacked safetensors or from the 1-bit GGUF (bonsai_interp.gguf_weights), whichever the folder holds."""
    from bonsai_interp.model import MODELS
    path = MODELS[name]
    if not (path / "model.safetensors.index.json").exists():
        from bonsai_interp import gguf_weights
        ts = gguf_weights.by_name(path)
        col = lambda L, n: gguf_weights.column(ts[f"model.layers.{L}.mlp.down_proj.weight"], n)
        return col, gguf_weights.dense(ts["model.norm.weight"]), gguf_weights.dense(ts["lm_head.weight"]).half()

# Graph schema

```
graph/
  contributions/<model>/L{L}_N{n}_{pos|neg}/
      <id>.tests.json     pre-registration, committed FIRST       (contributors write this)
      <id>.json           results, committed in a LATER commit    (written by `play run`)
  neurons/<model>/L{L}_N{n}_{pos|neg}.json     derived record     (written by `fold`, never by hand)
  edges.json                                   derived edge list
  index.json                                   derived summary for the site and the game
```

The model is `bonsai1` (Bonsai-8B, 1-bit): 36 layers, 12,288 neurons per layer, and two poles
per neuron.

## Contributions are append-only

A contribution is never edited, renamed or deleted after it is merged; CI rejects any PR that
does. A correction is a new contribution. Every record is recomputed from its neuron's
contributions in `(created, id)` order. This makes a merge **idempotent and non-destructive**:
merging the same contribution twice changes nothing, and new information never overwrites old.

`<id>` is `YYYY-MM-DD-<github handle>-<random suffix>`. Core-team history uses `core-…` ids.

### `<id>.tests.json` (the pre-registration)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `contribution`, `contributor`, `kind`, `neuron`, `protocol` | Who is testing which pole, and under which test protocol (e.g. `quick-8+8@1`) |
| `neighbours` | `[{"unit": "L12/N5397", "pole": "-", "label": …, "fire": [8], "quiet": [8]}]` |
| `qc` | For QC: `{"verdict": "confirm", "dispute" or "refine", "label_under_test": …}` |
| `predictions`, `short`, `unit_kind`, `confidence`, `notes`, `roles`, `via` | Optional. They are copied into the results |

### `<id>.json` (the results)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id`, `kind`, `neuron`, `contributor`, `created` | `kind` is one of `interpret`, `qc`, `replicate` (a blind clean-room run) or `map` (edges only) |
| `label` | For `interpret` and `qc` refine: the label that was tested |
| `qc` | `{"verdict": "confirm" or "dispute" or "refine", "label_under_test": …}` |
| `tests` | `[{protocol, tests_file, prereg_commit, author, …numbers…, per_sentence}]`. `counts_for_status: false` excludes a test from the status (used for model-written test sentences) |
| `recipe` | `{"toolchain_commit": …, "command": …}` |
| `edges` | `[{from, to, kind, weight, method}]` with full neuron ids |
| `artifacts` | `[{name, url, sha256, bytes}]` in the library |
| `short`, `unit_kind`, `confidence`, `depth`, `roles`, `via`, `examples`, `evidence`, `notes`, `verdict`, `summary`, `offshoots`, `lineage` | Optional |

## Protocols are versioned

`bonsai_interp/graph/protocols.py` maps each protocol to its pass rule:

- `quick-8+8@1`: held if at least 5 of 8 sentences fire at 0.3 or more of the pole's corpus max,
  and at most 1 near miss does.
- `quick-8+8@2` (the default for new tests): held if the fire sentences rank above the near misses
  (AUROC >= 0.90), the median fire sentence reaches 0.20 of the pole's corpus max, and at most 1
  near miss reaches 0.30. It needs the per-sentence activations that `play run` records.
- `held-out@1`
- `cleanroom@1`

A new pipeline adds a new version, such as `quick-8+8@2`. Old contributions keep the rule they
were made under. A test under a protocol the code doesn't know is kept and shown, but doesn't
change the status.

## How a record is folded

The record keeps the earlier fields: `id`, `label`, `short`, `kind`, `status`, `depth`,
`tests`, `label_history`, `examples`, `evidence`, `roles` and `contributors`. It adds
`contributions`, `qc` counts and `replications`.

| status | when |
|---|---|
| `unlabelled` | no contribution has tested a label yet |
| `held` | the latest round of the current label held |
| `contested` | the label held, but since it last changed, more QC tests have failed than held |
| `failed` | no label has held yet; one or two failed rounds |
| `unresolved` | no label has held after three failed rounds |
| `dense` | a contribution set `unit_kind` to a dense kind |
| `probed` | a full probe (`depth: full`) |
| `replicated` | only blind replications so far |

More rules:

- A failed round after a held label goes into `label_history` and does not replace the label. To
  challenge a held label, use a QC `dispute`, or a QC `refine` with a better label.
- `replicate` contributions never change the label.
- For list fields, the record holds the union of all contributions, in order. For scalar fields,
  the latest contribution wins.

## Read API

The derived files are the survey's public, read-only API. There is no server and no account: read
them from a clone, or over HTTPS from the `main` branch (once the repository is public):

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moridinamael/bonsai-interp/main/graph/index.json
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moridinamael/bonsai-interp/main/graph/neurons/bonsai1/L20_N12208_neg.json
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moridinamael/bonsai-interp/main/graph/edges.json
```

They change only when the merge agent folds a merged contribution, so a commit hash pins a snapshot.
Neuron ids are always `<model>/L<layer>/N<index><pole>`, e.g. `bonsai1/L20/N12208-`; record file names
are `L<layer>_N<index>_<pos|neg>.json`.

### `graph/index.json` (one object, about 1 KB per surveyed pole)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `models` | `{model: {layers, neurons_per_layer}}` | The models the ids refer to (only `bonsai1`) |
| `neurons` | `{id: entry}` | One entry per pole that has at least one contribution; poles not listed are unsurveyed |
| `neurons[id].status` | string | One of the statuses in the table above |
| `neurons[id].label`, `.short` | string or null | Current label (see "How a record is folded") and its short form |
| `neurons[id].kind` | string or null | `unit_kind`, e.g. `dense / positional`, `token/lexical` |
| `neurons[id].depth` | string | `quick` or `full` |
| `neurons[id].qc` | `{confirm, dispute, refine}` | QC counts |
| `neurons[id].n_contrib` | int | Number of contributions |
| `neurons[id].replicated` | bool | Has a blind clean-room replication |
| `neurons[id].contributors` | `[handle]` | In order of first contribution |
| `neurons[id].t` | `[[protocol, outcome, n_fire, n_false_pos, author, contribution id]]` | Every test, oldest first. `outcome` is `held`, `failed`, `invalid` (fields missing for its protocol), `recorded` (a protocol the code does not score) or, for `cleanroom@1`, the blind verdict in words |
| `neurons[id].history` | `[[label, outcome]]` | The last six labels tried |
| `neurons[id].scrutiny` | `{level, name, test_rounds, sentences, contributors, qc}` | How much evidence there is, 0 `unexamined` to 5 `replicated` |
| `edges` | `[[from id, to id, kind]]` | Every edge, without weights (those are in `edges.json`) |
| `contributors` | `{handle: points}` | The scoreboard, highest first |

### `graph/neurons/<model>/<pole>.json` (the full record)

Every field listed under "How a record is folded": `id`, `model`, `layer`, `index`, `pole`, `label`,
`short`, `kind`, `status`, `depth`, `tests` (each with its `contribution` and `outcome`), `label_history`
(`[contribution id, label, outcome]`), `examples`, `evidence`, `roles`, `contributors`, `contributions`,
`qc`, `replications` and `scrutiny`, plus the latest value of each optional scalar (`verdict`, `summary`,
`offshoots`, `lineage`). A record's `contributions` list names the files that produced it, so every
number can be traced to a pre-registered test.

### `graph/edges.json`

`{"edges": [{from, to, kind, weight, method, contribution, …}]}`, sorted, with the latest measurement of
each `(from, to, kind, method)`. `kind` is `feeds`, `reads`, `gates`, `co-fires` or an older free-text
kind such as `feeds lateral`; for `feeds`, `weight` is the share of the target's activation lost when
the source is zeroed.

### Not part of the API

- `site/cards.json` and the cards embedded in the survey page are label-free summaries of the corpus
  scan and the weights (top examples, density, regimes, direct logit effect) for surveyed neurons.
  Their compact format may change with the page; for any neuron, run
  `python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play card --neuron <id> --out card.json`.
- `data/token_index_bonsai1.npz` (token -> poles, used by `play which --token`) is a local artifact
  rebuilt from the scan on first use; it is never committed.

### Versioning

Field names above are stable. Changes are **additive**: new fields may appear at any level, and
readers should ignore fields they don't know. Status values and test outcomes may gain new values;
treat an unknown one as "not held". A change that renames or removes a field, or changes a field's
meaning, adds a top-level `"schema"` integer to `index.json` (its absence means schema 1) and is
announced in this file. Protocols are versioned separately (see above), so a test's numbers are always
read under the rule it was made under.

## Commands

```bash
python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play new interpret --neuron bonsai1/L12/N5397- --handle you
python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play run graph/contributions/bonsai1/L12_N5397_neg/<id>.tests.json

```

    commits = git("rev-list", "--reverse", f"{a.base}..HEAD").split()
    order = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(commits)}
    first, problems = {}, []
    for c in commits:
        for line in git("show", "--name-status", "--format=", c).splitlines():
            st, *paths = line.split("\t")
            derived = paths and paths[-1].startswith(("graph/neurons/", "graph/edges.json", "graph/index.json"))
            if paths and (st.startswith(("A", "C")) or (st.startswith("M") and derived)):  # a modified contribution must stay unrecorded here
                first.setdefault(paths[-1], order[c])
            for p in paths:
                if p.startswith("graph/contributions/") and (st.startswith(("M", "D", "R"))) and p not in first:
                    problems.append(f"{p}: contributions are append-only; it was {dict(M='modified', D='deleted', R='renamed').get(st[0])} in {c[:7]}")
    on_base = lambda p: subprocess.run(["git", "cat-file", "-e", f"{a.base}:{p}"], capture_output=True).returncode == 0
    total = 0
    tracked = set(git("ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "HEAD").split("\n"))
    for path, i in first.items():
        p = PurePosixPath(path)
        if path.startswith(("graph/neurons/", "graph/edges.json", "graph/index.json")) and not a.allow_derived:
            problems.append(f"{path}: derived file in a PR; drop it (git rm --cached) - the merge agent regenerates derived files on main")
        if path.startswith(("data/", "models/")):
            problems.append(f"{path}: nothing may be added under data/ or models/ (use the release or the library)")
        if path.startswith(("graph/", "runs/")) and p.suffix in (".json", ".jsonl", ".md", ".txt"):
            from bonsai_interp.graph.contrib import LOCAL_PATH
            body = git("show", f"HEAD:{path}") if path in tracked else ""
            if LOCAL_PATH.search(body):
                problems.append(f"{path}: contains a local path (e.g. C:/Users/<name>/…); redact it to ~ (DATA_POLICY: no local paths)")
        if path.startswith("graph/"):
            size = len(git("show", f"HEAD:{path}").encode("utf-8")) if path in git("ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "HEAD").split("\n") else 0
            total += size
            if size > MAX_FILE and path.startswith("graph/contributions/"):
                problems.append(f"{path}: {size // 1024} KB is over the {MAX_FILE // 1024} KB per-file cap")
        if path.startswith("graph/contributions/") and p.suffix == ".json" and not p.name.endswith(".tests.json"):
            c = json.loads(git("show", f"HEAD:{path}"))
            for t in c.get("tests", []):
                tf = t.get("tests_file", "")
                if on_base(tf) or (tf in first and first[tf] < i):
                    continue
                same = " (added in the same commit as the results)" if first.get(tf) == i else ""
                problems.append(f"{path}: pre-registration {tf!r} was not committed before the results{same}")
        elif path.startswith("probes/") and role(p.name) == "result":
            tests_here = [j for q, j in first.items() if PurePosixPath(q).parent == p.parent and role(PurePosixPath(q).name) == "test"]
            base_tests = [q for q in git("ls-tree", "--name-only", a.base, str(p.parent) + "/").split() if role(PurePosixPath(q).name) == "test"]
            if not base_tests and not any(j < i for j in tests_here):
                problems.append(f"{path}: no test file committed before it in {p.parent}")
    if total > MAX_TOTAL:
        problems.append(f"this PR adds {total // 1024} KB under graph/, over the {MAX_TOTAL // 1024} KB cap")
    for m in problems:
        print("PR CHECK", m)
    print(f"{len(commits)} commits checked, {len(problems)} problems")
    sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)
